sections.skill: Organize a complete case analysis and count or find every solution

questions.prompt: How many three-digit whole numbers (100 to 999) have digits that add up to 5?
A 12-hour digital clock shows times from 1:00 to 12:59: the hour (1 to 12, no leading zero) and then two minute digits (00 to 59). At how many times do the shown digits add up to exactly 22?
Find the two-digit whole number that equals 3 times the sum of its digits.
questions.rule: isInteger(n) and n >= 10 and n <= 99 and n == 3 * (floor(n / 10) + mod(n, 10))
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n >= 10 and n <= 99 and n == 3 * (floor(n / 10) + mod(n, 10)) (example: n = 27)

questions.prompt: In how many ways can you make 30 cents using nickels (5 cents), dimes (10 cents) and quarters (25 cents)? You may use any number of each coin, including none; the order of the coins does not matter.
Exactly 6 of the 24 orderings of the letters A, B, C and D have A before B and also C before D.

sections.relationship: Students who list cases at random miss some or count some twice. Ordering the list by one choice at a time makes it complete.
sections.author_note: Students who list cases at random miss some or count some twice. Ordering the list by one choice at a time makes it complete.

lesson.title: Make an organized list
text: Pick the choice with the fewest options and go through its values in order.
For each value, list what the rest can be, again in order.
When every value has been handled, the list is complete; count it.

example.title: Worked example (a different count)
prompt: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add up to 4?
steps: Go through the tens digit in order: 1 gives 13, 2 gives 22, 3 gives 31, 4 gives 40.
A tens digit of 5 or more is too big, and 0 is not allowed for a two-digit number. So there are 4.

questions.prompt: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add up to 6?
In how many ways can you make 20 cents using only nickels and dimes? The order of the coins does not matter.
There are exactly 4 two-digit numbers whose digits multiply to 12.
Ana lists the ways to make 15 cents from nickels and dimes: "3 nickels; 1 dime and 1 nickel." Is her list complete? The order of the coins does not matter.

choices.text: No: a nickel then a dime is a third way
No: 2 dimes and no nickels is missing
Yes: she used 0 dimes and 1 dime, and 2 dimes is too much

questions.correct_answer: Yes: she used 0 dimes and 1 dime, and 2 dimes is too much

questions.prompt: There are 5 two-digit numbers whose digits add up to 3.

sections.relationship: Harder: complete searches with several conditions.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: How many three-digit numbers have three different digits that add up to 6?
In how many ways can 10 be written as a sum of 1s and 2s if the order matters? (For example, 3 can be written 3 ways: 1 + 1 + 1, 1 + 2 and 2 + 1.)
Find a three-digit number whose three digits are all odd, all different, and add up to 15.
questions.rule: isInteger(n) and n >= 100 and n <= 999 and isOdd(floor(n / 100)) and isOdd(mod(floor(n / 10), 10)) and isOdd(mod(n, 10)) and floor(n / 100) + mod(floor(n / 10), 10) + mod(n, 10) == 15 and floor(n / 100) != mod(floor(n / 10), 10) and floor(n / 100) != mod(n, 10) and mod(floor(n / 10), 10) != mod(n, 10)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n >= 100 and n <= 999 and isOdd(floor(n / 100)) and isOdd(mod(floor(n / 10), 10)) and isOdd(mod(n, 10)) and floor(n / 100) + mod(floor(n / 10), 10) + mod(n, 10) == 15 and floor(n / 100) != mod(floor(n / 10), 10) and floor(n / 100) != mod(n, 10) and mod(floor(n / 10), 10) != mod(n, 10) (example: n = 159)

questions.prompt: There are more ways to make 50 cents from nickels and dimes than from dimes and quarters. The order of the coins does not matter.
How many rectangles of any size (including squares) can be traced along the lines of a grid that is 2 squares tall and 3 squares wide?

sections.relationship: Expert: split a large search into organized cases.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: A 12-hour digital clock shows times from 1:00 to 12:59: the hour (1 to 12, no leading zero) and then two minute digits (00 to 59). At how many times do the shown digits add up to exactly 6?
In how many ways can you make 1 dollar (100 cents) using nickels, dimes and quarters? The order of the coins does not matter.
How many positive whole numbers less than 1000 have digits that add up to 4?
Every whole number of cents from 8 to 30 can be paid exactly using only 3-cent and 5-cent stamps.
Give a whole number of cents from 1 to 10 that CANNOT be paid exactly using only 3-cent and 5-cent stamps.
questions.rule: n == 1 or n == 2 or n == 4 or n == 7
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: n == 1 or n == 2 or n == 4 or n == 7 (example: n = 7)
